the_words: we should review all the skills and workflow every month until we can't find anything to improve.
the_standing_practice: Every month, review ALL eleven skills and press_office/WorkflowDefinition.md as one pass. TERMINATION IS STATED IN THE RULING AND IS NOT A DATE: the cadence ends when a review finds nothing to improve. So a review that returns empty is the exit condition, not a wasted pass — which means an empty result must be recorded as loudly as a full one, or the practice cannot end.
what_it_subsumes: The loose '/summarize revisit' date (notes/2026-08-11-a-hand-called-context-door-fires-twice.json, 'well, in a month we can revisit', landing 2026-09-11). Both of the things that revisit hung off — the /summarize idea and the /moreabout firing measurement — are skills-layer, so review #2 is that revisit. The one-off date becomes an instance of a standing cadence, which is the correct direction: a date in a file was already flagged in that note as the same shape as the problem it was measuring.
nothing_fires_this_yet: MEASURED AND STATED PLAINLY: this decision is a date in a file. bin/cmd/slate --hook is the event that already fires every session (troubles, gate, lap), and a due-lane there is the event-driven answer — never a cron. NOT BUILT. Until it is, this cadence runs on somebody remembering, which is the exact failure mode /moreabout's 2-firings-in-14-days measures. Ticket owed.

review_1.scope: 11 skills (challenge, chart, commit, design, idea, intent, moreabout, note, sail, saveslate, sorted) + press_office/WorkflowDefinition.md
instruments: bin/cmd/skilldial — firings, refusals, findings, match rate, last fired, per skill
ls ~/.cairn/devices/chart/0/packets — per-stage berth counts, the chain-attrition curve
a field census over every intent berth — challenge presence and from_idea presence by date
a Law 5 census over skills/*/ — proofs, state, history, validations, door
green_measured_not_asserted: THE CHALLENGE FLOOR HELD. 19 of 19 intent births since it shipped carry all five answers; the 7 without it are all dated 2026-08-01..08-03, before the door judged the field. The ticket challenge-fires-at-intent worked: an optional route that fired 3-in-10 became a required field that has never once been missing since.
THE from_idea EDGE HELD. Every birth from 2026-08-06 onward resolves to a real ideas record or carries 'none, because <X>' with a referent. 16 of 16.
CHART CHAIN COMPLETION IMPROVED. 41 orient -> 32 verdict = 78%, against 64% measured 2026-08-04 (25 -> 16). The chain is leakier at the top (orient 41 -> constrain 38) than anywhere else.

findings.what: skills/sail/intention+why.json declares counted_by.what_it_counts = 'NOTHING. /sail is the one skill in the roster that leaves no firing record anywhere. Measured 2026-08-04, after checking every store the other ten are counted in: no berth, no packet, no trace...'. That is false, and was false when written. ~/.cairn/devices/chart/0/packets/verdict-*.json holds 32 records, the earliest 2026-07-29 — one per /sail voyage that reached step 6, and the emit chokepoint REFUSES the PROVED crossing without a complete passing verdict artifact (ExitGateRed). So the record is not merely present, it is MANDATORY.
findings.why_it_matters: This is a recurrence of the exact error WorkflowDefinition §6 already caught and retired on 2026-08-04 — 'not being JUDGED AT A DOOR was silently read as not being COUNTED, and those are different facts.' That repair fixed five skills and skipped the sixth, and the sixth is the build step: the most expensive firing in the workflow, and the one the charter itself calls 'the worst place for it'. The lesson did not transfer to the case that motivated it.
findings.the_honest_caveat: A verdict berth counts sails that reached PROVED. A /sail that reads berths and builds nothing, or dies mid-voyage, still leaves nothing — so this is a FLOOR that undercounts, and it must say so in what_it_counts, exactly as commit's git-trailer proxy declares that it overcounts. It does not fully close the charter's own 'a /sail that shipped and one that didn't look identical' complaint; it closes the half that is measurable today.
findings.disposition: TICKET. Not a charter edit alone: counters._read_files globs *.json in a directory and offers group_by_prefix (which groups but does not filter), so pointing sail at chart's packets dir would count all 294. It needs a prefix filter on the reader plus a proof case, then sail's charter declares reader=files, address=instance/devices/chart/0/packets, prefix=verdict-. That is a build on a proved component, so it goes through /intent -> /sorted -> /chart -> /sail.
findings.law_7: The false claim is NOT deleted from the charter when this is fixed. It is marked superseded with the date and the measurement that killed it — a record of truth keeps its errors.

findings.severity: found while fixing the one above, and sharper than it
findings.what: cairn/skill_block/counters.py::count() lines 253-257: when a charter declares reader='none' it returns the HARDCODED string 'no store — this skill leaves no firing record anywhere. Not a gap in the roster: a gap in the system, declared in the charter rather than implied by a dash.' That sentence is a claim about the WORLD, minted by the counter, for any charter that declares no reader.
findings.why_it_matters: reader='none' means THIS CHARTER DECLARES NO READER. It does not mean NO RECORD EXISTS ANYWHERE. The module collapses those two facts into one sentence and asserts the stronger one — which is the roster's own falsifier turned on the roster: 'unmeasured is not zero', and this is unmeasured being printed as measured-absent. It is also why Akien's instruction could only be half-carried out at the charter: sail's text is corrected, and bin/cmd/skilldial goes on printing the same false sentence for it, because the sentence was never sail's to begin with.
findings.disposition: TICKET, merged with the one above — one ticket, 'the roster can see /sail', two parts: (1) count() must report the charter's silence as silence and print the charter's own what_it_counts where one exists, never a minted world-claim; (2) _read_files gains a prefix filter so sail can declare address=instance/devices/chart/0/packets, prefix=verdict-.
findings.the_transfer_worth_naming: this is the third instance today of one shape — a true local fact (no reader declared / not judged at a door / no band ordering asked for) restated as a stronger global one, and then read back later as established. It is worth the review asking that question directly next month rather than stumbling on it.

findings.what: /design fired 7 times. /sorted fired 33. WorkflowDefinition §1 declares design as one step with a different skill at each end — /design opens the joint work, /sorted closes it. Measured: the close ran 26 times on a session that never opened.
findings.why_nothing_notices: /sorted's 12-field contract, read live from its charter, contains no citation to a design berth. So the design->sorted edge is the one edge inside the citation half of the catalog that does not exist. WorkflowDefinition §1's citation table cannot see it either, because that table has one row per STEP and design is one step with two doors — the table's own shape hides the missing edge.
findings.the_mechanism_measured_2026_08_11: DESIGN IS A DEAD-END LIMB. Its INPUTS are five fields, of which one is a judged citation: intent_berth (must resolve, must be an intent berth, must have exited routed_forward, or a 'none, because <X>' with a referent); entering_from (intent | sorted:<berth>); open_questions (a LIST, not a paragraph); ready_when; bullets. Its OUTPUT is exactly one berth under instance/devices/skill_block/0/berths/design/ — no commons artifact by charter ('the artifact of the design STEP is the cast ticket, and /sorted writes that') and deliberately no exit field. AND NOTHING DOWNSTREAM ASKS FOR THAT BERTH: /sorted's twelve fields carry no design reference, and of 108 tickets, 42 carry intent_berth, 33 carry sorted_berth, and 2 carry design_berth — a field in no contract at all. So the step consumes a citation and emits one nobody requires. That is the whole mechanism of the skip: there is no door and no gate anywhere that a missing design berth would fail.
findings.its_one_real_consumer_and_where_it_stand: probes/design_return_trip.py (WATCHME(design-return-trip), ticket the-return-trip-is-countable, armed 2026-08-07). It fires when >= 12 distinct nodes show zero recorded returns. Measured today: 7 berths, 7 distinct intent_berths, all seven entering_from='intent', ZERO returns ever recorded — and the seven fall on just two days (four on 2026-08-07, three on 2026-08-11), so the pattern is burst-when-remembered, not use-then-abandon. The probe is at 7 of 12 and on current evidence will fire and report exactly what the charter feared: the back-edge has never been travelled.
findings.the_open_question_this_forces: Is /design optional in practice and the doc wrong, or is the doc right and the step is being skipped? Both readings are live and they lead to opposite fixes (drop the step, or add the citation from /sorted). The measurement does not settle it — and note that the probe firing will not settle it either: 'no returns recorded' is equally consistent with a step nobody runs and a step that never needed a second pass. This is a design question.
findings.disposition: TICKET, and the ticket's first job is to put that question to the question corpus rather than to guess it.

findings.what: A census of skills/*/: chart and moreabout carry a charter and a SKILL.md and NOTHING ELSE — no proofs/, no state.json, no history.json, no validations/. sail has state and history but no proofs. commit and note have a proofs/ directory containing a PROOF.md and no runnable teeth, and no validations/ — never sealed.
findings.why_chart_is_the_sharp_case: chart is the most-fired skill in the system (294 firings across eight doors) and the longest artifact (551 lines of SKILL.md). Law 5 says intent, its voyage, and its proofs share an address. Chart's intent is at its address; its voyage and its proofs are not anywhere. WorkflowDefinition §6 already says 'chart's gate is unreadable from here... the most-gated step in the workflow is the one this document can see least of' — that was written about its contract, and the same hole is wider than the doc claimed: it is the whole Law 5 triple, not just the contract.
findings.the_part_that_is_not_a_defect: commit and note are prose skills and a PROOF.md may be the right shape for a human-proved class (/sorted: 'the reviewers are the verdict and the notary is the seal'). The absence of validations/ means no seal was ever written by either hand. That is a question, not a finding — raised as one.
findings.disposition: TICKET for chart's address. The commit/note seal question goes to the question corpus.

findings.what: /moreabout: 2 firings, both 2026-07-28, none in the 14 days since. Full measurement and its consequence for the /summarize design already recorded at notes/2026-08-11-a-hand-called-context-door-fires-twice.json.
findings.disposition: no new action — it is review #2's subject by the subsumption above.

findings.what: orient 41 -> constrain 38 -> survey 39 -> decompose 37 -> triage 37 -> hypothesize 35 -> validate 35 -> verdict 32. Where a chain dies is a directory listing. WorkflowDefinition §6 named this red on 2026-08-04 ('a second finding nobody built anything to read'). Still true 7 days later, on a larger sample.
findings.the_shape_worth_noticing_and_what_it_cos: survey (39) exceeds constrain (38), which cannot happen in a strictly forward chain. RESOLVED BY MEASUREMENT RATHER THAN LEFT AS AN ALARM: all 39 survey packets carry a constrain_ref, all 38 constrain berths on disk are cited, none dangles, and exactly one berth (constrain-20260802T164817-8fd5ce2138d0.json) is cited twice — by survey-20260802T165050 and survey-20260802T165150, sixty seconds apart. So it is a same-minute re-fire of one stage, which is normal motion, not a broken chain. THE FINDING IS THE COST: establishing that took a hand-written script today, and a reader of the curve would have said it in one line. An unread instrument does not only hide failures; it makes ordinary motion look like a defect until someone pays to prove otherwise.
findings.disposition: carried to review #2 as an open red, with the re-fire resolved here so it is not re-discovered as an anomaly from scratch.

review_1.what_this_review_did_not_cover: Efficacy. skilldial reports match rate for the five door-judged skills (intent, saveslate, sorted all 100%; design and idea have no verdicts recorded yet) and a dash for the other six. A 100% match rate across three doors is not evidence the doors are well-tuned — it is consistent with a door that never disagrees with anything. Naming it as uncovered rather than reporting it as green.
